El Abd · Master presentation · mockup for sign-off, built on a branch, not live yet

A guided tour of one direction's slides

Before the directions present, one of them is used as the example. The slides are dimmed and one part is lit at a time, with a card saying what that part is. These are real screenshots of the build, on the demo company shaped like El Abd: four directions, D001 named after yours. The figures are invented.

1. Pick the direction in the flow

A new Guided tour line under the two lists in Master presentation. It offers only what is in the flow, so it lists directions, capabilities, units or functions, whatever the client has. Take a direction out of the flow and the tour goes with it.

2. Press Guided tour on its cover

The picked direction's cover carries a Guided tour button in the corner. Pressing it, or G on the keyboard, starts the tour. The button is never printed in the PDF.

3. The tour, stop by stop

Fourteen stops across four slides, then a closing card. Click a stop, use the buttons, or the arrow keys here, the same keys the presenter uses in the room.

    4. How it behaves in the room

    ActWhat happens
    → or the clickerLights the next part. When a slide's parts are done it moves to the next slide by itself.
    Click on the dimSame as Next, so a mouse or a tablet drives it too.
    ←Back one part, across slides if needed.
    G or the ×Ends the tour and stays on the slide you are on. The deck carries on as normal.
    A part that is not thereSkipped. No categories slide, no delayed tactic or no execution reading means that stop is left out, so the same tour works on any direction, unit or function.
    The wordsThe client's own: "direction", "Key measures", "Tactics", and the scoring bands as set in Setup.

    To decide

    • Which direction for today. Pick one with a delayed tactic if you want the DELAYED stop. Without one, that stop is skipped.
    • The direction appears once. The tour runs on that direction's own slides where it sits in the flow. Drag it to first place so the example comes before the others. Showing it twice (once as the example, once in its turn) is possible but would take longer to build.
    • The pick is kept on this browser only. If you present from another laptop, pick it again there.
    • Escape in full screen leaves the deck. The browser takes Escape first, so use G or the × to end the tour.
    • The card wording is on each screenshot above. Tell me any line to change.
